_meta.description: YouTube RPM and CPM benchmark data aggregated from verified creator-facing sources
_meta.methodology_note: Data aggregated from OutlierKit (AI+human curated niche data, updated monthly), Lenos/LenosTube (creator report aggregations), upGrowth industry reports, and MilX market analysis. RPM = creator earnings per 1,000 views after YouTube's 45% revenue share and accounting for non-monetized impressions. CPM = advertiser cost per 1,000 ad impressions before platform cut. No source has direct YouTube Analytics API access — all figures are aggregated from creator-submitted dashboards, public disclosures, and research panels. Treat all values as benchmarks, not guarantees.

rpm_shorts.notes: Shorts RPM is fundamentally different from long-form: the Shorts Feed ad pool is shared across all videos, and YouTube allocates the resulting revenue by watch-time share. Expect 50-100x lower RPM than equivalent long-form content. Source: Influencer Marketing Hub YouTube Shorts RPM report.

cpm_by_country._metric: CPM (advertiser cost per 1,000 ad impressions, all-niche average unless noted)
cpm_by_country._note: RPM ≈ CPM × 0.45–0.55 after YouTube's 45% platform share and non-monetized view discount

countries.notes: upGrowth 2026 data. Leads Tier 1 markets. Small creator base relative to audience size keeps competition high.

seasonal_multipliers._source: Lenos platform-wide CPM trend data (Dec 2024 peak $6.93, Jan 2025 trough $1.98); OutlierKit seasonal guidance

quarters.notes: Advertiser budgets reset after Q4 holiday spend. January 2025 platform CPM hit $1.98 — the year's trough. New-year fitness, tax, and finance verticals partially offset the slump.
Gradual recovery. Travel and outdoor-lifestyle advertisers ramp for summer planning season. Finance remains elevated through tax season (April).
Back-to-school spend in August/September lifts tech and education CPMs. General summer slump in broad entertainment niches.

Peak advertiser competition for holiday and year-end budgets. Lenos: Dec 2024 averaged $5.70 platform-wide CPM; Cyber Week peak $6.93. Finance and credit card advertisers reach $30-$45 RPM. Q4 premium is most pronounced in high-intent niches (finance, retail, tech).

rpm_vs_cpm_explainer.cpm: Cost Per Mille — what the advertiser pays per 1,000 ad impressions. Set by auction.
rpm_vs_cpm_explainer.rpm: Revenue Per Mille — what the creator actually receives per 1,000 video views. Always lower than CPM.
rpm_vs_cpm_explainer.gap_explanation: The CPM→RPM gap has two components: (1) YouTube keeps 45% of ad revenue; (2) not every video view results in a monetized ad impression (ad-blockers, skipped pre-rolls, non-monetized regions). In practice RPM ≈ CPM × 0.45–0.55.
rpm_vs_cpm_explainer.example: A $10 CPM typically delivers ~$4.50–$5.50 RPM after platform cut and non-monetized view discount.
